attributes.provenance: src/game/enemy/critter.c CritterInitHeader semantic reconstruction (work_claim.critter-initheader.20260831.v1, worktree GDL-Claude-CritterHeader); attempt.critterinitheader-record-reconstruction.20260830.v1. Every field in this record was cross-checked against the actual `*(u16/u32/f32*)(p+0xNN) = CritterSwapNN(...)` statements in CritterInitHeader before trusting any prior struct's padding claim.
attributes.scope: Any TU with a byte-swap/endian-fixup function (WAD/file loaders, network/save deserializers) walking one or more fixed-stride on-disk records; the swap statements are ground truth for exactly which byte ranges hold real numeric fields vs. genuine padding/text, independent of and prior to any earlier reconstruction's struct comments.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: A per-record byte-swap loop (the `CritterSwap16/32/F` family here, or any equivalent endian-fixup) enumerates EXACTLY the byte ranges of an on-disk record that hold real numeric fields -- every offset it touches is a field boundary and width; every offset it skips is either text (untouched by byte-swapping) or genuine unused padding. This makes the swap loop strictly more reliable than an EARLIER reconstruction's struct comments/pad-array claims for the SAME record, because a prior pass can mis-classify a real field as padding (declare `u8 _padXX[N]` over bytes it never checked a consumer for) without any build-time signal -- the pad array still compiles, sizes correctly, and gates byte-identical, since nothing else in the TU reads through it. This session found FOUR such over-claims in critter.c alone, none caught by any prior gate because a gate only proves the CURRENT source is byte-exact, not that a padding claim is honest: (1) CritterSfxRecord's `levelFmt[0x24]@0x20` claimed text through 0x44, but the swap loop proves real floats start at 0x30 (color[3] via CritterDoSfx) -- the true text run is only 0x10 bytes. (2) CritterColDescriptor's `_pad18[8]`/`_pad40[4]` were real swapped floats (unk18/unk1C/unk40) with no consumer found in-TU. (3) CritterPattern's `_pad30[0x20]` was a full CritterTargetCriteria embed (8 real floats), reachable because CritterChildCriticalMove passes `pattern+0x30` to the same CritterGetTargetSub the move-record's identical block feeds. (4) CritterPackedType's `_pad060[0x40]` and `_pad0AC[0x48]` together hid ~24 real fields (look-at yaw/pitch rate/bias pairs, the type-level CritterTargetCriteria, speed/floorOffset/damageScale/armor/turnLimit/maxHealth/expValue and more) with roughly a third having direct consumers elsewhere in the TU and the rest genuinely unreferenced (named unkNN rather than left as blind padding, since they still had to be individually swapped). A near-miss the SAME session almost repeated: converting CritterDamageDef's swap loop from memory of an EARLIER struct's `_pad18[4]` claim before re-reading the exact swap statements would have silently dropped the real `mindp` field at 0x18 -- caught only by re-verifying the raw swap-loop text line-by-line against the struct being written, not by any build/gate signal (a dropped-but-still-compiling field is invisible to `defake_gate.py check` if nothing else in the TU independently constrains that byte). Consequence: before trusting ANY existing struct's `_padXX[N]`/`unk` block for a record that has a byte-swap loop somewhere in the TU, re-derive the record's real field boundaries from the swap loop's own offset list first, then reconcile -- treat the swap loop as the authority and the prior struct comment as a hypothesis to verify, not the reverse. Where the swap loop proves a real field but no consumer is found anywhere in the TU, name it (`unkNN`/`fNN`, following the file's own convention) rather than leaving it in an unswapped-looking pad array -- future readers need the field-boundary information even when semantics remain unknown.
